summary: PAPER-SCHROER-23 is a careful extraction, and its review found a real error in the paper. I re-verified by hand, with Tate's algorithm in characteristic 2, that the three Jacobians the review adds to Theorem 10.4 (I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁ and IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂) exist, have split additive fibres and Σn_a = 25, and satisfy §10's hypotheses. So the gap in Theorems 15.1 and 5.1 (E44) stands. The 16 library citations resolve at the pins, the 15 planned statuses match their stage texts, the Proposition 5.5 repair is sound, and the errata record's eleven mistakes are all carried over. The work breaks in seven places. (1) The E44 gap was not carried into the items built on it: items 119 and 130 still state the printed configuration tables as theorems, item 146 carries a 'proof checked' note, and item 47 and the report do not mention the gap (high). (2) Route 4 was accepted on 23 September. R07.1 was then planned and closed on 28 September without this source, so the route will never be applied, and R07.1 now plans items 52 and 54 (medium). (3) R25.3, closed on 28 September, plans π₁(Spec ℤ) = 1 (item 181) and the simple 2-groups over ℤ, so route 7 duplicates it (medium). (4) Enriques surfaces are defined in two pending new roadmaps (this one and Benoist's RealSurfacePeriodIndex), and K3 surfaces are used with no import of K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness (medium). (5) Proposition 8.1's cited inputs, EGA IV 18.5.11 and Raynaud's Théorème 8.2.1, have no item (medium). (6) The mistakes are registered twice, under colliding ids E1–E11, with conflicting reach, and without sourceVersions (medium). (7) Item 215 misdescribes JacobianChallenge Layer D, and route 1 should build on it (low). 7 findings: 1 high, 5 medium, 1 low.

The review's main finding re-verified by hand. For the three added models y²+txy+t³y=x³+x², y²+txy+t³y=x³+tx² and y²+txy+t²y=x³+t²x², I computed b₂, b₄, b₆, b₈, Δ and j in characteristic 2, ran Tate's algorithm at t = 0 (including the coordinate change and the splitting of the final quadratics, which shows that all components are rational), found the tangent cones at ∞ (non-split), counted the t = 1 fibre (E₄), and checked Σn_a = 25 and condition (ii) of §10. All three are confirmed. The exhaustive 2²¹ search behind 'exactly three more' was not repeated. I noted that the review's point-count check (Σ#J_t = 1+10q+q²) cannot by itself detect non-split additive fibres, which is why I checked the components with Tate's algorithm. I also checked that the paper's IV* elimination (Proposition 11.3, p. 37) does not cover IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂.

findings.claim: The review found that Theorem 10.4 misses three Jacobians and recorded that this leaves a gap in the proofs of Theorems 15.1 and 5.1 (E34, E44). It changed item 115, the route briefs and the summary, but did not carry the correction into the items that depend on it. Item 119 still says the rational-fibre configurations of an elliptic fibration on a constant-Picard Enriques surface over F₂ are 'exactly among' the eleven configurations of table (12). E44's own correction says the three configurations I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁ and IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂ must be added to that column. Item 130 says every genus-one fibration on a non-exceptional such surface has one of 'these' eight configurations. None of Propositions 11.2–11.3 treats the three new configurations, so 130 is not established either. Item 146 (Theorem 15.1) carries the review note 'Proof checked: … /130, /133, /142, /143 leave I₁*+E₄+I₄ … or I₂*+III+III'. That contradicts E44, which the same review confirmed. Item 47's note lists its dependencies without the open step. The report's overview still says the proof 'classifies eleven elliptic equations … reduces fifteen possibilities to eight'. A design job building nodes from 119 and 130 would state lemmas that the source does not prove and that may be false. I checked that the three models exist and satisfy the hypotheses of §10 (see evidence), so the gap is real. I also checked that the paper's own IV* elimination does not cover IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂. The proof of Proposition 11.3 (p. 37) uses the table to put the other multiple fibre in 'Kodaira symbol III or IV'. In the new configuration it is the smooth fibre E₄.
findings.evidence: Paper: arXiv 2004.07025v3 (SHA-256 ae6481f2…6d61), p. 33, Proposition 11.1: 'the possible configurations of fibers over the the rational points t = 0, 1, ∞ are given by the following table'. p. 38, Proposition 11.4: 'the possible configurations … are given by the following table' (eight entries). p. 37: 'we may assume that ϕ⁻¹(0) = 2(C′₀ + … + C′_{r−1}) is multiple with Kodaira symbol III or IV'. p. 31, the twisted case: 'Now (11) becomes r_a + i + r_c = 11 … and the argument is similar', followed by a list with only two twisted configurations. My hand check of y² + txy + t³y = x³ + x² over F₂: b₂ = t², b₄ = t⁴, b₆ = t⁶, b₈ = a₂a₃² = t⁶, so Δ = b₂²b₈ + b₆² + b₂b₄b₆ = t¹⁰ and j = a₁¹²/Δ = t². At t = 0 the change of variables s = 1 gives (a₁,a₂,a₃,a₄,a₆) = (t,t,t³,t³,0). Tate's algorithm gives P(T) = T²(T + 1), then Y² (double root), then X² + X = X(X + 1) with roots in F₂. So the fibre is I₂* with all components rational, and n₀ = 15. At t = 1, y² + xy + y = x³ + x² has 4 points. At ∞, ord Δ = 2, the node of y² + xy + y = x³ is at (1,1), and its tangent cone Y² + XY + X² is irreducible over F₂, so the fibre is Ĩ₂ and n_∞ = 6. Total 25, and condition (ii) holds. For y² + txy + t³y = x³ + tx²: Δ = t¹¹, j = t, and at 0 the sequence is T²(T+1), Y², X², Y(Y+1), which gives split I₃*; there is Ĩ₁ at ∞; 17 + 4 + 4 = 25. For y² + txy + t²y = x³ + t²x²: Δ = t⁸(t² + t + 1), and at 0 P = T³ and Y² + Y = Y(Y+1), which gives split IV*; Ĩ₂ at ∞, I₁ at the F₄-point; 15 + 4 + 6 = 25. In PAPER-SCHROER-23.result.json: item /146 note, 'Review note: Proof checked: every genus-one fibration of Ȳ descends (/68) … leave I₁*+E₄+I₄ (I₁* multiple) or I₂*+III+III'. sourceIssue E44, correction: 'Add the configurations I₂*+E₄+Ĩ₂, I₃*+E₄+Ĩ₁ and IV*+E₄+Ĩ₂ to the elliptic column of (12) … and exclude them … before concluding'.

findings.claim: Route 4 has never reached its owner, and it is now partly a duplicate. The review accepted the route on 23 September 2026 (commit e210f8f4). The FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory blueprint then planned R07.1 in its first checkpoint (commit e8b22985, 28 September 2026) and closed it (packet coverage: R07.1 'closed', remaining []). The paper appears nowhere in that packet, and the released issue #731 lists no added source. So R07.1 was closed without Schröer, and a source route into a closed stage will not be acted on. Meanwhile R07.1 now plans two of the four items. (1) Item 52: node R07.1/oort-tate-classification classifies finite locally free groups of order p over any Λ_p-scheme by triples (L, a, b) with a ⊗ b = w_p. For p = 2, Λ₂ = ℤ[1/2] ∩ ℤ₂ = ℤ, so every scheme qualifies. (2) Item 54: node R07.1/oort-tate-over-number-rings, part (iii) (Artin–Mazur), says 'Over ℤ the only group schemes of order p are ℤ/pℤ and μ_p'. What R07.1 does not state is the paper's explicit rank-two form. That covers item 51 (the coordinate group law f₁ ⋆ f₂ = f₁ + f₂ − b f₁f₂, whose sign the paper misprints, E5) and item 53 (Cartier duality (L, a, b) ↦ (L⁻¹, b, a) for general L). The node gives duality only as G_{a,b}^∨ = G_{b,a} over rings with Pic R = 0. Items 52 and 54 are therefore wrongly 'missing', and 51 and 53 need a request to the closed stage, not a source route. Disclosure: this session (cc-f805bf) reviewed PAPER-BREUIL-CONRAD-DIAMOND-ETAL-01, whose routes go to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.1 and R07.4. This finding rests only on the R07.1 packet, the git dates and issue #731, not on that review.

findings.claim: Two new roadmaps planned in parallel both define Enriques surfaces, and Schröer's routes use K3 surfaces without importing their owner. (1) Route 6 (EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence) plans item 26, the definition of Enriques surfaces in every characteristic. PAPER-BENOIST-19 route 9 (new roadmap RealSurfacePeriodIndex, accepted on 23 September 2026, after this extraction's review) plans item PAPER-BENOIST-19/114. That item defines 'An Enriques surface in characteristic 0 … with H¹(O)=H²(O)=0 and canonical bundle nontrivial of order 2' and its canonical étale K3 cover. DESIGN-EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence and DESIGN-RealSurfacePeriodIndex are both pending, and neither brief names the other. The definition and the canonical cover would be built twice. The two definitions are also not the same: Benoist's (characteristic 0, torsion of order 2) is Schröer's specialised through Proposition 4.2. PAPER-BHATT-MORROW-SCHOLZE-18 route 9 (CP.5, 'Enriques surfaces in characteristic 2 have nonzero H¹_dR') and PAPER-BENOIST-WITTENBERG-20 route 5 (MC.7, 'Enriques Picard torsion input') also consume the notion. (2) Items 148 ('No K3 surface X/Q has good reduction over W(F_pbar) for every prime p') and 188 ('its canonical G-torsor is a smooth connected K3 surface') use K3 surfaces. No item defines them, and neither the route 3 brief nor the route 6 brief imports K3SurfacesAndSymplecticBoundedness. That is the accepted new roadmap for K3 geometry (PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22 route 3; its brief 'reuses the new-roadmap candidate proposed by PAPER-CHARLES-16 for K3 geometry', whose item 1 defines K3 surfaces). findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-SCHROER-23.result.json: item PAPER-SCHROER-23/81 (Proposition 8.1) and route 2; no item for the cited inputs
findings.claim: The proof of Proposition 8.1 (the isogeny E_k ~ (X_k)_red that gives Corollaries 8.2–8.3 and hence J_a ≅ (Y_a)_red in Proposition 11.1) rests on two cited theorems that have no item. The first is EGA IV 18.5.11: over a henselian DVR, an effective Cartier divisor on the closed fibre of a flat scheme extends to an effective Cartier divisor on the total space, here a regular one finite over R. The second is Raynaud 1970, Théorème 8.2.1: a proper flat morphism with a section is cohomologically flat in dimension 0, which the paper uses to get h⁰(O_C) = h¹(O_C) = 1 for the closed fibre C of the modification Y → Spec R′. The proof also uses the construction of a normal model Y dominating both X′ and E′ and the valuative lift D ⊂ X′, which item 81 states nothing about. Item 81 has no note naming these inputs, and none of items 189–245 (the review's coverage additions) covers them. A search of the extraction for '18.5.11', 'cohomologically flat' (outside /211) and 'Théorème 8.2.1' finds nothing.
findings.evidence: Paper (arXiv v3), p. 22, proof of Proposition 8.1: 'This is an effective Cartier divisor, and can be extended to an effective Cartier divisor D_k ⊂ X_k on the fiber. In light of [29], Theorem 18.5.11 we may extend further, and regard it as the closed fiber of some effective Cartier divisor D ⊂ X.' and 'According to [52], Theorem 8.2.1 the morphism Y → Spec(R′) is cohomologically flat, because it admits a section. In turn, the closed fiber C = Y ⊗_{R′} k′ has cohomological invariants h⁰(O_C) = h¹(O_C) = 1.' References: [29] EGA IV₄ (Publ. IHÉS 32); [52] Raynaud, Spécialisation du foncteur de Picard (Publ. IHÉS 38). Item /81 has statement only and no note.
findings.fix: Add two missing items on route 2 (GenusOneFibrationsAndRationalEllipticSurfaces), both importing SchemeAndStackFoundations. (a) 'Lifting effective Cartier divisors over a henselian base (EGA IV 18.5.11)': for X flat of finite presentation over a henselian local ring R and D₀ ⊂ X_k an effective Cartier divisor finite over k, there is an effective Cartier divisor D ⊂ X, finite over R, with D ⊗ k = D₀. (b) 'Cohomological flatness in dimension 0 (Raynaud 1970, Théorème 8.2.1)', stated with Raynaud's own hypotheses, taken from the source: X proper and flat over a DVR with X normal and O_S = f_*O_X, and the multiplicities of the components of the closed fibre with gcd 1, which a section guarantees. The conclusion is that f is cohomologically flat in dimension 0, so the closed fibre has h⁰ = 1. Record in item 81's note that its proof uses (a), (b), Lemma 8.4 (/84–/85) and a normal model dominating X′ and E′.

findings.claim: Item 215's note says 'tauceti JacobianChallenge Layer D records the Br-flavoured obstruction only for curves with a section'. Layer D does not say that. It sets up the relative Picard functor for any f : X → Spec k that is proper, flat and finitely presented with geometrically integral fibres. It records the Br-flavoured obstruction between Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) and Pic_{X/k}(T) in that generality, and only then rigidifies with a section. It also names the 'General Picard scheme of a projective variety (Hilbert/Grothendieck)' as a representability route. So the geometrically integral case of items 213 and 215 lies within a Tau Ceti layer. Schröer needs arbitrary proper X, possibly non-reduced or disconnected, with H²(S, h_*G_m) = Br(X_aff) in place of Br(k). Route 1's Part II is still justified for that generality, but its brief should start from Layer D and not re-plan the integral case. As written, the brief imports only A0-extension and SF.
